change: No changes. Primary (Lats/Latissimus Dorsi, mid back/Rhomboids+Lower Traps, shoulders/Posterior Deltoid) and secondary (biceps, Rotator Cuff, obliques, Lower Back/Erector Spinae) are all confirmed correct for a standing unilateral mid-cable row. Obliques as secondary confirmed by EMG research on unilateral rows.

Added oblique (External Obliques + Internal Obliques) as secondary. Per the rules, unilateral standing exercises engage obliques for anti-rotation stability, and the standing resistance band variation especially demands core anti-rotation. The existing primary (Triceps/Triceps Brachii) and other secondaries (shoulders/Anterior Deltoids, abs) are confirmed correct — the arm is held overhead in shoulder flexion requiring anterior deltoid stabilization.

No changes. Muscle data is appropriate for a standing unilateral low cable row. Low cable position emphasizes lats; posterior deltoid, rhomboids, and lower traps are primary movers in the rowing pattern; biceps, rotator cuff, obliques (anti-rotation, unilateral), and erector spinae (standing stabilization) are correct secondaries.

No changes. Holding a single dumbbell with both hands in a supinated grip is a biceps curl variation. Biceps Brachii is the clear primary mover; Wrist Flexors are engaged for grip. Brachialis and brachioradialis cannot be mapped to any allowed bucket/latin, so they are correctly omitted.

Moved Quads (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Lateralis) from primary to secondary. The single kettlebell deadlift is a hip-hinge dominant movement; glutes and hamstrings are the true prime movers (hip extension), while quads assist with initial knee extension off the floor. Multiple sources including NASM and kettlebell-specific guides confirm this. All other entries retained: Lower Back, obliques (anti-rotation for unilateral carry), forearms (grip), Lats (spine stabilization during hip hinge).
